## R6: WON's Internet code, round 18 (every routing op, request and notification, as one Rust object)

Branch `rust-won-net18`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 17. Round 17 left WONRouting's request helpers
and its 55 op classes (the requests, the notifications, the derived server's op): RoutingLogic and EEWonNet read their
members class by class, so the readers moved with them.

- **What moved.** `routeop.rs` (`EeWonRouteOp`): one Rust object per op of any type (`RoutingOpType`), with every
  member the op classes had as a numeric field by number (`EE_WON_RTF_*`, each with its member's width: an assignment
  is cut as the original's was), four texts (`EE_WON_RTT_TEXT` / `NAME` / `PASSWORD` / `COMMENT`, UTF-16 units), the
  data type, the data buffer (none for a null `ByteBufferPtr`), the recipients, and the records its replies build
  (clients, members, groups with their members, data objects, bad users, the joined client: shared records as the
  original's `SmartPtr`s, so a member's client made after the member went in its map is that member's). Every step:
  the constructors' defaults, `SendRequest` (the members it resets, the message from routemsg.rs's `request`,
  whether the op waits in the connection's list: not a chat or data send without flag 1, never a disconnect), and
  `HandleReply` (routemsg.rs's `reply`, its assignments applied as `WONRoutingMsg.h`'s templates applied them, a cut
  short read, `RoutingCreateGroupOp::CheckLeaveGroup`'s leave), `ParseGroupListObj`, and the group list request op's
  replies read again (`RouteGroupListOf`, now `ee_won_routeop_read_group_list_of` straight from the Rust host op).
- **The C++ left.** `RoutingOp` is the one class: the `AsyncOp` the connection's list and the completions hold, its
  type a constructor argument; `RunHook` (blocking mode refused), `SendMsg` (the length field) and `AddOp` stay, and a
  leave op is run where the Rust read asks for one. Accessors: `Num` / `SetNum`, `Text` / `SetText`, `DataType`,
  `GetData`, `Recipients`, and copies of the records into new C++ maps (`GetClients`, `GetMembers`, `GetGroups`,
  `GetDataObjects`, `GetBadUsers`, `GetClientInfo`, `GetGroupInfo`) through one record sink. `RoutingDetectFirewallOp`
  keeps its listening socket as a subclass. `RoutingGetUserStatusOp` (a UDP op on the lobby lane's manager) stays,
  with the slim `WONRoutingMsg.h` it uses; the rest of that header is test glue now (`tests/won/won_routemsg_glue.h`
  for won_routemsg_test and won_reqlast_test, which still check routemsg.rs's C ABI against the original
  statements). The record factories `GetNewClientInfo` / `GetNewMemberInfo` / `GetNewGroupInfo` are gone.
- **The readers.** RoutingLogic's 20 notification handlers, its create, join, ban, mute, bad user, register and group
  list ops, and EEWonNet's callbacks read the accessors and copies (`LobbyServer::SyncClients` / `SyncGroups` take the
  copied maps unchanged). The smart connection's `RoutingOpCompleteHook` is one call (`ee_won_smart_routeop`: the
  model reads the Rust op's fields and records itself), and its `ee_won_smart_put_*` / `ee_won_smart_op` are gone.
- **The golden over real loopback sockets.** `won_routeops_test` (new, `xbuild wontest`): a plain RoutingConnection to
  a routing server stand-in on 127.0.0.1; every request helper and the ops RoutingLogic builds itself, the bytes the
  server receives, the replies (statuses, lists, records, a members reply for another group, a join that waits, a
  password retry on the same op, a create with its join status), every notification type and a derived message,
  each finished op dumped through every member its readers use; a group list body read by a connection-less op.
  Recorded over the unmodified classes (534 lines, six runs the same, `golden_routeops.txt`, its own commit), then
  replayed over the Rust ops through the accessors (`EE_WON_ROUTE_OPS_RUST` picks the path): 534 lines, 0 failures.
  won_servconn_test (202), won_smartroute_test (668), won_routemsg_test (4,256,706 checks) and won_reqlast_test
  (90,093 checks) pass unchanged; servconn's golden names op classes, so the driver maps the types it meets to them.
  Mutations: a chat without flag 1 added to the list fails line 523; a group list's members dropped fails line 58.
- **Driver trap.** An op run again after it finished (RoutingLogic's join password retry) sent its request twice in
  one run of six when rerun at once: the driver pumps 50 ms before the rerun. Not a port difference (the original
  classes did it).
- **Behaviour.** The original's uninitialized members (a notification's fields before its read, the register op's
  client id from its long constructor, the members op's observer count before a reply) are 0. A record's text
  crosses as UTF-16 (identical on Windows; on Linux and macOS a lone surrogate stays one unit, as `WideAssignUtf16LE`
  keeps it). A data object's or op's buffer read back is a copy, not the same `ByteBuffer`.
- **Net C++** (src+include, the generated headers left out): +808 -4355; of the deletion about 680 lines are
  `WONRoutingMsg.h`'s templates moved to the test glue. 17 units and 3 headers deleted; WONRouting.h -866 +49,
  RoutingConnection.cpp -662 +313, RoutingOp.cpp +241 -43, SmartRoutingConnection.cpp -119 +3.
- **LAN reach: none.** RoutingConnection and its ops are made only by an Internet login (the lobby's RoutingLogic
  `ConnectToServer`, EEWonNet's server select); the WON servers are gone. Every LAN lobby and game runs on the lobby
  lane's sockets and LanLogic, and EE-SIM never makes a routing op. The driver and the Rust tests exercise it.
- **Not moved, and why.** RoutingGetUserStatusOp (UDPManagerSendRecvOp's subclass: the lobby lane's object). The
  RustServerOp host (ServerOp.cpp's HostCall): still answers on C++ objects. ServerConnectionConnectOp (four short
  members over the connection).

## R5b.4, twenty-first round: the location goal whole in Rust (ee_units location.rs; branch rust-r5b4-core21, 2026-11-13)

| Commit | What | C++ (src, include/ee) |
|---|---|---|
| e69d3b7c | merge of `rust-combat14` (the heal goal on EEUGRust, no longer an `EEUGLocation`) | |
| 0283763c | the location goal whole in Rust (`EEUGLocation` deleted; 51 caller files) | +353 -648, net -295 |

- **The most used goal, the same pattern.** `EEUGLocation` (every move order, the group paths' slots, forced moves,
  facing on arrival, the automatic waypoints) is an `EEUGRust` of kind `kGoalLocation`. Its seven members are one
  `#[repr(C)]` record by goal object (`EeUnitsLocationGoal`); the bodies are location.rs: the four constructors (one
  body operation, 480: the point, the yaw and the flags in the argument block; the `(bool, ...)` load constructor
  passes 0, 0, 0, yaw 0, no facing), `Clone` (the group movement flag copied, as the original's), the dump, the
  checksum, the debug texts, `GetGoalLocation`, `Start`, `Save`, `Load` (five version branches folded into one
  sequence of version tests: the same reads in the same order), `EvaluateCondition` and `FaceYaw` (481). The base
  goal's answers (`GetDestination` told to the group, three path attempts, `Suits` true, the empty `Step`, `SetOwner`,
  `Abandon`, `ReplaceUnit`, `RepairPointers` 0) come from the dispatch's defaults or the body's empty arms.
- **The accessors read the record without the host.** The callers (the physics models' `Step5` every tick, the path
  manager, the active group, the client, the AI) read and write the members through `EEUGRust` accessors with the
  original names (`GetLocation`, `SetLocation`, `GetYaw`, `GetIsForcedMove`, `GetShouldFace`, `GetIsAutoWaypoint`,
  `Get/SetUseGroupMovement`, `Get/SetGroupPathState`), each one copy of the record out of (and back into) the table
  through `ee_units_location_goal_get` / `_set`: no host callback, no dispatch. `GetLocation` now returns by value
  (no caller bound the reference). `EELocationGoalCast` replaces `EEGoalCast<EEUGLocation>`, `dynamic_cast` and the
  kind-tested `static_cast`s; `new EEUGLocation(...)` became `EEUGRust::NewLocation(...)` with the same four
  argument lists (a script did the 51 files: the class name, the casts, the include). The goal class cast template
  of `EEUnitKind.h` went with it (no goal class is a C++ class of its own any more).
- **FaceYaw in Rust over ee_ge.** The original's arithmetic (the forward vector through the unit's transformation,
  `UMArcTan2`, the half-turn wrap, the one-degree test, `SetOrientationYPR(yaw, 0, 0)`) already forwarded to ee_ge
  in C++ (`GETransformation::SetOrientationYPR` -> `ee_ge_t_set_orientation`, `UMArcTan2` -> `ee_ge_um_arctan2`, the
  header's inline `Apply(vector)` restated in its order as `apply_vector`), so the Rust body calls the same functions:
  the host only hands over the unit's `GETransformation` (64 bytes through `io.sink`, `static_assert`ed) and takes the
  turned one back (`SetTransformation(t, true)`). Host operations 490-494: the class category, the transformation in
  and out, `SetTargetSearchTimer`, the first goal queue's length. The unit update's `FACE_YAW` action calls the same
  body. Clippy rejects the literals `3.1415927` (`approx_constant`): `f32::consts::PI` and `TAU` are the same bits.
- **Combat's four helpers** (`EELocationGoalPoint`, `EESetLocationGoalPoint`, `EELocationGoalYaw`; `EEGoalHasLocation`
  unchanged) take their location branch from the accessors. The heal goal's own copy of the facing test
  (`EEHealLocationCondition`, combat's, at yaw 0) is left as it is.
- **An include removed above its first use.** The script dropped `ee/EEUGLocation.h` wherever the file already
  included `ee/EEUGRust.h`; in `EESMEffect.cpp` that include came 1,600 lines below the first `NewLocation` (one
  compile error; the include now stands where the old one was).
- **Coverage by temporary prints (removed): the first sight of each body and branch, one file per process.** Oracle
  seeds 2-7, the scenario profile seeds 2-7 and saveload's oracle, islands and space games (seed 2, 1000 s) reach:
  creation, `Destroy`, `GetGoalLocation`, `GetDestination`, `GetStartAction`, `Start` (the timer reset, prepare to
  move for ground units and aircraft), `EvaluateCondition` (facing done both ways, facing not required with and
  without the facing flag, the base fallback for the rest), `FaceYaw` true and false, `SetOwner`, `Abandon`,
  `ReplaceUnit`, `PathTaken`, `SetPathAttempts`, `Save`, `Load` (0.280) and `RepairPointers`, and the accessors (get
  and set). No game reaches `Clone`, the dump, the checksum (the oracle's `oos` is not the goals' sum), the debug
  texts, or `Start` on the location itself (turn to face or idle): unit tests only (location_tests.rs, 6 tests).
- **Only a tour reaches:** the client's location commands (`EEClient` 0xb8-0xba with a location goal), the command
  confirmation's waypoint flags (`EEE3DCommandConfirmation`), the graphical goal manager's auto-waypoint test, the
  debug panels' location texts, and the test fixture's order checks (`EETestFixtureOrders.cpp`). No goal is ever
  encoded on the wire (the messages make their goals on each side), so the LAN game's codec is unchanged.
- **Behaviour:** none on the games' paths. The members of the load constructor's goal that it left unset in the
  original (`mLocation` before `Load`) were already 0, 0, 0 (`GE3DPoint()`).
- **Gates.** On 0283763c (the branch is `rust` 37a013f7 plus combat round 14; `rust` had not moved): build `--sim`
  and the test profile link 0/0; oracle seeds 2-7 identical to the main checkout's `ref`; the Rust gate PASS (ee_units

## R5b.2, fifteenth round: the drop location, the hit distance and the map's unit regions in Rust (ee_combat leaves.rs, regions.rs; branch rust-combat15, 2026-11-13)

Measured by net C++ deletion (src and include/ee, git numstat).

| Commit | What | C++ |
|---|---|---|
| 0ee808ac | `EEFindDropLocation` and `EEGetHitDistanceSquared` whole in Rust over the world host | +65 -71, net -6 |
| d4bb3958 | the map's unit regions a Rust table (`EEMap::mUnitRegions`), its 26 C++ sites on it | +152 -233, net -81 |

- **The drop location and the hit distance.** leaves.rs `find_drop_location` and `hit_distance_squared` are the
  original's statements over the world host: the active goal's kind (`mActiveGoal`, not the store's `mGoalState`),
  its location and its attack target, the target model's drop point (`GetModel()->mModel`, `mDefaultPoint`), the
  tile's height and a unit's virtual `GetPosition` (a simple unit's tile centre) are new reads and operations
  (Q 88, H 10, W 70-73); the scale, built flag, hit points, maximum and location were reads already. The CBDP and
  CBHD records are written from Rust at the original's places (the target's id from the store's `Q_ID`), so the
  goldens recorded from the C++ in round 2 and 4 gate the move: oracle, calamity and late at seeds 2-3 equal. The C++
  names stay one-line forwarders (fifteen callers: the bombs, helicopters, air animals, landables, missile physics,
  the drop calamity, the unit AI). `ee_combat_drop_point` and `ee_combat_hit_distance` had no caller left and went.
  The predecessor's estimate held: the move is about even in C++ lines (the host cases cost what the body saved);
  `EEPointArgs` folds the operations' point outputs to keep it from growing. `FireShot`'s `W_FIND_DROP` still calls
  the forwarder: calling Rust directly would re-plumb the drop point into three launch operations for no deletion.
- **The unit regions: a Rust object the map owns.** `RTSRegionTable<EEComplexUnit*>` was one instantiation of a
  template the influence table and the effect regions keep, so the template stays; `EEMap::mUnitRegions` is now an
  `EeCombatUnitRegions*` (`ee_combat_regions_new`/`_free` where the map made and deleted it: two maps keep two
  tables, no global). Regions are `Vec<u64>` (C++ pointers) in the original's column-major array; `add` appends,
  `remove` erases the first copy (order kept), `values` walks the regions from the last and each from its back,
  `collect` sorts by handle and dedups (the original's `std::less` on pointers), `footprint` is the fortress
  footprint's add or remove (the original's single-region branch was the loop's one pass). Off-grid tests stay

## R4.4, fourteenth round: an effects sweep against the original C++, two bugs it found, the water splash and screen flash whole in Rust (ee_gfx effect_aged.rs; branch rust-gfx20, 2026-11-13)

Graphics Thread C++ (`src/Empire Earth/Graphics Thread/*.cpp`): 21,867 lines before the round; 22,008 after the
sweep (+140 TEST ONLY, +1 the load fix); 21,643 after the water splash and screen flash (-365).
`EEE3DWaterSplash.{h,cpp}` and `EEE3DScreenFlash.{h,cpp}` deleted.

- **Coverage first: the effects sweep.** Round 13 measured that no gate game makes most of the moved 3D kinds. EE-SIM
  `--effect-sweep` (sim_capture `--profile effects`: the oracle's game cut at 600 game seconds) holds every capture
  record from the start (`EESimCaptureRecord::Hold`, new) and, when the game ends, runs `EEEffectCaptureSweep`
  (`EEEffectManager.cpp`): each of 14 kinds (0x18 blast wave, 0x1b water splash, 0x21 tracers, 0x23 disease, 0x25
  3D projectile, 0x26 shells, 0x27 additive pass, 0x33 citizen beam, 0x3f teleport, 0x42 virus, 0x43 pulse cannon
  ball, 0x44 time warp, 0x45 shield, 0x46 screen flash) is made through each entry point that makes it (on a unit,
  at a point, between units, unit to point, between points) from the first two graphic effects of its kind, on the
  newest unit on the map of the first two players with one; the effect detail raised to every level for it. 0x43
  and 0x44 have no row in the data: they borrow the first blast wave's and teleport's rows (the row's kind set for
  the creation only). Each case: three manager updates, the effect saved, a load-time effect of its kind loaded from
  the bytes, repaired and saved again (the copy kept out of the manager: `ReleaseResources`, then leaked; the game is
  over), forty updates, the effect destroyed. EFSW is one record per case (the creation's result, made, lived, the
  load's and repair's results, both saves' lengths and FNV-1a, the first save's bytes); EFST and EFMU after every
  update. 26 cases, 1,144 updates a seed.
- **Its golden is the original C++'s.** The sweep's patch applied to f839d277 (the commit before round 11: all 14
  kinds C++, the timed effects' steps too) in a temporary worktree under `build/` (its own staging root), built and run
  at seeds 2-3: `tools/sim_capture/golden_cpp_effects.txt`. The game itself is the same there (EFMU equal at once), so
  every difference was an effect's. The worktree was removed after.
- **Two bugs the sweep found, each its own commit before the golden:**
  - `EEE3DRust::Call` gathered the graphic facts, the unit's hit points among them, before every op. A load runs
    before `RepairPointers`, when `mUnit` is still the saved unit id: loading a saved game holding any moved kind on a
    unit (blast wave, teleport, time warp, shield, citizen beam, shots) read through the id and crashed (the sweep's
    first run: an access violation in `Call` from `Load`). Load and Save now build only the host and call the file op.
    No gate game saves one of these kinds, so the saveload matrix never met it.
  - The citizen beam's line: the original's `mLine` was a default `GE3DLine` (direction (1, 0, 0)) until `Aim`; the
    record started it at zero, so an unaimed beam saved direction 0 (EFSW's first-save bytes showed the four bytes).
    Round 13's driver missed it: its stub `GE3DLine` had no default direction. Lesson: a stub world's default
    constructors must be the engine's; the sweep against the real C++ catches what a driver's stubs hide.
  With both fixed the current tree gives the golden's 6 digests (and every EFSW record) at seeds 2-3: the eight kinds
  moved in rounds 12-13 now match their original C++ in a real game world, made, stepped, saved and loaded.
- **The water splash (0x1b) and the screen flash (0x46) whole on `EEE3DRust` (`effect_aged.rs`).** The splash is
  made at a point (`CreateAt`), loads its media in `SetUp`, queues in 4 with its age, draws in pass 6 (eased growth
  from the start size, the eased age written back, flattened by `1 - age^2`, faded over the last tenth); the flash
  zeroes its age when made, takes its complex unit's position in `SetUp` (a new host call: `mComplexUnit->GetPosition`,
  not the unit's virtual), draws in pass 6 the standing plane at the camera's orientation, additively, dimmed by the
  fog factor and `1 - age^2`, in front of everything through the main viewport's depth range 0..0 (restored to 0..1,
  z writes and less-equal after). Both age by `aged_step`; Load and Save ignore the base's and media's results. The
  facts gain `start_size`; the rasterizer table the camera (`gRenderSnapshot.mCamera`), the standing plane
  (`gEffect2DModel`), the depth range with `SetViewport`, `SetZCompare`, the material's opacity and a post-model
  transform scaled by `GETransformation::Scale` (the engine's, in the C++ lambda). The water splash's draw age is the
  aged record's `draw_age` now (it was a C++ member).
- **Golden driver** (`build/gx20/aged`: both classes cut verbatim from HEAD against `EEE3DRust`'s host,
  constructors and `Call` and the rasterizer table cut from the worktree over the Rust; the world is round 13's beam
  driver's generated stub world plus the viewport, z compare, camera, plane and material opacity): 300 effects
  (6,639 lines) and 3,000 on seed 2 (67,608 lines), identical. Rust tests: 4 (`effect_aged_tests.rs`), and the beam's
  line default in `effect_beam_tests.rs`.
- **Behaviour:** two fixes (the load crash; the unaimed beam's saved line direction, back to the original's). The
  moves change nothing (the effects golden, recorded from the C++, passes after them).
- **Gates.** On the result merged with rust (93edfb38): `build.py --sim` and the test profile link 0/0, the Rust gate PASS (2,642 tests), the sim oracle identical on seeds 2-7, the captures at seeds 2-3 PASS (oracle 169 digests, late 170, calamity 183, effects 6; TNMT without a golden as always), `saveload --settings all --seeds 2-3 --at 1000,1900 --expect tools/saveload_expect.txt` PASS (the matrix as expected). Per commit: the load fix the build 0/0 and the oracle at seeds 2-3 identical; the aged move the build 0/0, the oracle at seeds 2-3 identical, the effects capture PASS, the Rust gate PASS. The aged driver was run on the move's commit, not rebuilt after the merge (the merge touched no file it cuts). No tour run.
- **Only a tour or a person reaches:** the two draws through the new table entries (the splash's eased, flattened,
  fading model in pass 6; the flash's in-front quad, its depth range and z compare restored after: a wrong restore
  would show as the scene drawn over the UI or z fighting after a flash), and loading a saved game that holds a moved
  kind on a unit (the fixed crash: the sweep loads copies, not a whole saved game).
- **Next:** the additive pass (a redraw of its unit's model: host calls for the unit's model, stats scale, frame and
  animation), the linear projectile, the disease and virus with their orbitals; the sweep already records all four
  from the C++, so each move is checked against the original in a game world; a 2D twin for the sprite effects.

    default handling instead of being dropped: nothing opens an MCI device, so none arrives.

    `RecordCaller` had no caller) and `ESProfile` (every member an empty inline body; the history map nothing filled).
  - `link/lle/units.txt` lost the four units' lines.
- **ISDeviceInput whole in Rust** (`rust/crates/ee_input`, commit 2, -229): the device buffers the port wrote in
  place of DirectInput 7 (PORT.md step 4.4): the 256-record buffer and its overflow flag, the key bytes, the mouse's
  motion and buttons, acquire/unacquire, and `ISHandleEvent`'s event switch (scan codes, `PlatWindow` buttons to
  DirectInput's order, the wheel's `lrintf(notches x 120)`, a focus loss letting go of every key and button). The two
  system devices are Rust statics (`ee_input_system_init` / `_device(0|1)` / `_shutdown`); `ISKeyboard` and
  `ISMouse` keep an opaque `ISDeviceInput*` (`typedef EeInputDevice`) and call `ee_input_*`. `ISMouseState` and
  `ISInputRecord` are now the Rust records under their old names (`typedef EeInputMouseState`, `EeInputRecord`,
  with DirectInput's field names `lX`, `dwOfs`, ... so `ISMouseAxis`'s pointers into the state and every reader
  compile unchanged). `ISHandleEvent` is one C++ line passing the event's type and both union views' fields; the
  Rust reads only those of the event's type.
  - **The golden** (`tests/input/is_device_golden.cpp` over `tests/input/is_device_orig.h`, the class and the
    event switch copied unchanged from 5d3ce6a9): 20,000 sequences of 30-90 random calls (events through
    `ISHandleEvent` with one system device sometimes absent, acquire/unacquire, buffer reads with random counts and
    NULL, key and mouse state reads, direct calls with out-of-range scan codes and buttons, bursts of 100-350 moves
    that overflow the buffer): 1,206,926 trace lines, 309,525 result lines, all equal in the Rust replay
    (`EE_INPUT_GOLDEN=<file> cargo test -p ee_input long_run`). Seven Rust mutations fail it: a 255-record buffer
    (947 sequences), acquire keeping the motion (2,703), a key recorded without a change (10,703), right and middle
    swapped (5,858), the mouse state keeping its motion (4,552), the overflow reported twice (3,555), a focus loss
    skipping key 0xff (1,898); the restored source: 0. `golden_input.txt` (the first 40 sequences) is replayed by
    `cargo test`. The wheel values stay under 1,000 notches in the golden: past 2^31 / 120 the original's `long` is
    32-bit on Windows and 64-bit on LP64, so the indefinite value and the sum's overflow differ by system (a unit
    test pins x86's indefinite value; arm64's `lrintf` saturates there, which no device reaches).
  - **Behaviour:** none on the traced paths. The device lock is a Rust `Mutex` (the original's `PlatMutex`); no
    call holds it across a call out.
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM never creates the Input System, and the deletions are unreachable code: the oracle stays
  identical by construction (seeds 2-3 identical after each commit). The input devices run in every windowed game:
  the lead's tour (`fixture_game.py`: the clicks and key presses go through `ISHandleEvent`, the F3 input check, the
  arrow-key scroll and the zoom keys) is the check; a focus loss, the wheel and a buffer overflow run only in the
  golden unless a person uses them. The save path's twin deletion runs in EE-SIM's saves (the saveload matrix).
- **Left, in the order this census suggests:** `ISKeyboard`/`ISMouse` with their entities (`ISKey`,
  `ISExtendedKey`, `ISMouseButton`, `ISMouseAxis`: virtuals the UI's hot keys read); the Error System
  (Filter.txt's filters, the native error, `ESVerify`; its error log is opened and never written); `FSPersistentList`
  (a tag -> prototype map over C++ objects); `ESChecksum` (embedded in `EEGameState` and subclassed by
  `EEPChecksum`: a Rust object with a copy); `TMPoll`/`TMTimer`; the thread system over PlatThread; then the File
  System's `FSFileSpec`/`FSPath`/`FSArchive` walk and the Sound Engine's object side, which need `UString` and the
  FSFile virtuals across first. The string classes (`UString`, `UWideString`, 1.2k lines, used by every unit) are
  the largest single piece and the last.

## R6 WON round 31: a NULL-receiver audit of the moved classes; the child layouts whole in Rust (ee_won layoutobj.rs; branch rust-r6-won31, 2026-11-13)

Measured as rounds 18-30 (every file under `src/Empire Earth/WONAPI` and `include/ee/wonapi` at the commit, `wc -l`):
80,092 at the branch's start (round 30's head merged with rust) -> 80,096 (the hardening, +4) -> 79,917 (the child
layouts, -179). This round's own net: -175.

- **The audit (its own commit first).** Round 30's crash came from a forwarder reading its Rust object through a
  NULL `this` where the original returned before touching `this`. A NULL `this` only survived a non-virtual call
  (a virtual call reads the vtable) whose original body, on some path, read nothing of the object. Scanning every
  moved class's Rust methods for an early return decided by the arguments alone (ctobj, dialogobj, tabobj,
  comboobj, rootobj, btnobj, barobj, scrollerobj, paneobj, listobj, inputobj, labelobj, textobj, splitobj,
  multiobj, treeobj, menuobj) found:
  - `Container::BringToTop` / `EnsureOnTopOf` / `RemoveChild` / `AddTimerChild`: the child's parent compared with
    `this` (no read). RemoveChild and AddTimerChild are virtual; EnsureOnTopOf's one caller tests the parent;
    BringToTop's (the dialog's drag, `t->mParent->BringToTop(t)`) runs only with a next sibling, so with a parent.
  - `RootContainer::AddBG`: round 30's fix.
  - `Button::IsDefaultButton`: a pointer compare; its callers pass live buttons.
  - `ListArea::GetItemPos(NULL)` and `InputBox::Add/SetInputHistory("")`: every receiver is a member set at
    construction or a tested cast.
  - `MultiListItem::SetItem` and `MultiListHeader::SetColumnItem` with a negative column: undefined in the original,
    not a NULL path.

  No live caller passes NULL. Two host ops whose safety rested on the Rust's own test now guard explicitly: the
  dialog's `DlgBringToTop` (a NULL parent) and the viewport's `VpAreaRectVisible` (an area never set: not visible).
  A guard must sit at the call site: clang assumes `this` is not NULL and drops an `if (!this)` inside a method.
- **Why the layouts this round.** They are the next leaf under Container (every container owns a manager), with no
  platform call and no draw, so a golden sees all they do. Window/WindowManager are mostly platform calls, popups
  and the modal stack, and their callers reach them through `GetRoot()`, which is NULL for a component outside a
  window (the round-30 hazard at its largest); the skins' Button subclasses are paint only the lobby captures see.
- **The census.** No layout member was read outside the layout units: `mGroupId` and `mEnabled` only by
  `Container::AddChildLayout` (moved), the lists and numbers only by the classes' own methods. The lobby makes the
  classes (`new CenterLayout(...)->Add(...)`, ContainerConfig's LAYOUT keywords, the message box, the error screen)
  and hands them to `AddChildLayout`. Nothing needed an accessor, so there was no census commit. Before moving, the
  callers' receivers: ContainerConfig's `mContainer`, the dialogs, `this`; `mChildLayout` is NULL only after the
  container's destructor deleted it, when every child's parent is already cleared.
- **The move** (`layoutobj.rs`):
  - `EeWonLayout`: one Rust type for the eight classes (`EeWonLayoutKind`), with five references, eight ints, two
    flags, the component list, the group (a byte) and the enabled flag. Its constructor's numbers come as one
    `EeWonLayoutInit`. Execute is each class's statements; every read is made where the original made it, after
    the moves before it (Center and NoOverlap read a listed component's place at its move, so a component listed
    twice reads its moved place).
  - `EeWonLayoutMgr`: the instructions (held, each with its Rust object) and the layout points (held). Execute
    reads the list again after each call (an instruction appended meanwhile runs, as the `std::list` walk ran it).
    The destructor releases the points first, then the instructions (the members' reverse order); Clear releases
    the instructions first.
  - `Container::AddChildLayout`'s statements (the group stored as a byte, group 0 enabled and run before the
    manager holds it, any other disabled) and `PercentLayoutParam::DoCalc` moved; `CenterLayout::Center` runs a
    Rust centre layout with no C++ object.
  - The C++ classes are reference-counted shells: the base holds `mLay`, a subclass constructor makes it, `Add`,
    `Execute` and `UsesComponent` forward. `PercentLayoutParam` stays C++ (its `SetBorders` already called the
    Rust rule); `PercentLayout`'s constructor hands its anchors and numbers over. Four ops (560-563): the parent
    read, `SetSizeAtLeast`, an instruction's `AddRef` / `Release`; the reads and moves are the existing `Child*`
    ops. ChildLayouts.cpp is the host; CenterLayoutExecute.cpp and CenterLayoutStatic.cpp are deleted.
  - Every op is on a component or instruction passed in: a layout object never reads its own shell, so a NULL
    shell cannot be read through.
- **The golden** (`tests/won/won_layoutobj_test.cpp`): the original statements, copied before the change, over a
  world of 14 components (1 the container, 2-9 its children, 10 a grandchild so a reference is sometimes the
  child's parent, 11-14 layout points). A size change of the container runs its manager again one level deep
  (Container::SizeChanged), so a layout that grows its own container re-enters the manager mid-walk. Moves and
  references are traced; reads answered from the world.
  - The original's `push_back` of a raw pointer into a list of `SmartPtr`s makes a temporary (an extra hold and
    release); the copy uses `emplace_back` so the trace shows the lasting references only.
  - 20,000 sequences of 40 calls, 3,003,344 trace lines, all identical, every reference given back.
  - Seven mutations fail it: Center reading every place before moving (2,796 sequences), the destructor releasing
    the instructions first (13,325), RemoveComponent skipping the instruction after an erased one (93),
    AddChildLayout holding before its first run (20,000), NoOverlap moving the list before the target (9,838), the
    group not truncated to a byte (4,646), the percent layout's right edge without the width (11,253). The restored
    source: 0, and the mutation run had ended before anything else ran (round 29's lesson).
  - `golden_layoutobj.txt` (40 sequences) is replayed by cargo: the replay makes each line's call on the Rust
    objects over its own copy of the world and compares the whole trace (no op-by-op answers); it fails on a move
    changed by one.
- **Lesson:** clippy's `not_unsafe_ptr_arg_deref` rejects a `pub fn` taking a raw pointer it dereferences: take a
  reference and dereference at the FFI dispatch.
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM never builds the lobby, so the oracle is unchanged by construction (seeds 2-3 identical).
  Every lobby container runs its layouts through `layoutobj.rs` at each size change: the lead's LAN game
  (`lan_game.py`: every screen laid out at lobby entry, the game room, the dialogs centred by `CenterLayout::Center`)
  and the lobby captures (every control's place and size, the percent and same-size layouts of the skins'
  resources) are the check. A window resize relayouts everything; only a person resizes the lobby window.
- **Left:** Window/WindowManager (platform ops; audit every `GetRoot()->` caller first), the skins' Button
  subclasses (draw ops), the remaining WONGUI controls' C++ paint.

## The merge of main daf9dadb into the rust branch (the Lua AI's tower sites, walls and production queues; 2026-11-13)

49 commits of main (since a2c4347e; 21 files: `ai/classic_lua/walls.lua` and `build.lua`, `boom.lua`, `lib/place.lua`,
`lib/build_order.lua`, `ais.json`, AI_RESEARCH, the CI release workflow) merged into `rust` as `git merge origin/main`
(branch rust-mainmerge3). The C++ classic AI stays as it is: main's `EECPResourceManager.cpp` change (gather
`exact = 2` and `granary_farms`) acts for next-engine seats only.

- **Both lines took the next state's version 4.** The one conflict was `EECPNextLua.cpp`'s state block, which is Rust
  here (ee_ai `next_save.rs`): rust's version 4 is the site walkers (save 0.274), main's version 4 the
  `granary_farms` setting (§8.51). Main's field went into the Rust block as version 5 (version 4 plus the field; below
  5 it reads -1, the engine's rule). The EENS golden still checks the driver's version 4 bytes: the test drops the
  newer fields before comparing (`golden.rs as_v4`). As at the earlier merges: read both sides' version gates, not
  only the conflict.
- **Main's `gather(exact)` was not saved.** `EECPNextState::mExact` ("transient, the next order sets it") reset to 0
  on a load, and until the script's next gather order the rebalance kept one gatherer of slack. Main's `ais.json`
  makes the random Boom play `boom_order` (exact = 1 every step), so the saveload test's next games parted 10 ticks
  after the 1900 s loads. Saved since (version 6, its own commit): next seed 2 1000 s 114 -> 887 equal ticks, 1900 s
  10 -> 51, seed 3 1000 s 102, 1900 s 10 -> 888. The rest is a gap in main's new Lua state, not measured further.
- **The oracle.** Line 0 changes on every seed (the manifest: `4 AIs (boom, ...) folder hash df82b2b8`, was
  `5 AIs (boom, boom_order(not random), ...) 1494ba43`); every other decision line and every checksum line equals
  `ref` (seeds 2-7). With the previous tree's Data/ai (1494ba43) the merged exe is identical to `ref`, line 0
  included: the C++ and Rust side changed nothing for the classic seats.
- **saveload_expect.** Every row but the four next rows is as before (no row better or worse). The next rows are
  re-read with the tree's Data/ai main's; with the previous Data/ai the merged exe (before the exact fix) gives the
  old 479/END/828/END.
- A fresh worktree's first `build.py` failed at the link (`build/clang/exe/link.rsp`: `link_exe` does not create
  `exe/`); creating the folder by hand was enough.

| Commit | What | C++ (src, include/ee) |
|---|---|---|
| 2768ba64 | `EEUGRust` merged into `EEUnitGoal` (no vtable, `EEUnitGoal.cpp` deleted); the base record's Save and Load in Rust | +280 -537, net -257 |
| 39d29081 | the radius searches and the footprint tests in Rust (world.rs) | +45 -159, net -114 |
| 8749c5d5 | the gathering: `BeginGathering`, the work tick, the naval search in Rust (world.rs) | +41 -119, net -78 |
| 340c84e9 | merge of `rust` (combat 15, renderer 14, LLE 1, WON 31): no conflict | |

The round's C++: net -449 (the +280 of the first commit is mostly the class declaration moved from
`ee/EEUGRust.h` into `ee/EEUnitGoal.h`).

- **One goal class.** Since round 21 every goal kind was an `EEUGRust`, the only subclass of `EEUnitGoal`. The two
  are now one class, `EEUnitGoal` (ee/EEUnitGoal.h), with no virtual function: each of the original's 30 slots is a
  plain member that makes one call of the kind's Rust body (or, for the trivial ones, reads a field). `EEUGRust`
  stays as a typedef so its 95 caller files (`EEUGRust::NewLocation`, `EERustGoalCast`, the combat lane's
  EEUGRustCombat.cpp) compile unchanged; the three headers that forward-declared `class EEUGRust` now declare
  `class EEUnitGoal; typedef EEUnitGoal EEUGRust;`. The constructor (the id from `sGoalCounter`, the game time) and
  `CreateGoal` moved into EEUGRust.cpp; `RemovedFromQueue` (empty in every class) is an inline no-op;
  `link/exe/units.txt` lost EEUnitGoal.cpp's line.
- **A non-polymorphic delete is now well defined**: with a single class, `delete` of an `EEUnitGoal*` runs the one
  destructor (the Rust `DESTROY` body). Before the merge a derived class without a vtable would have been undefined
  behaviour, which is why the two names became one class and not a base plus an empty subclass.
- **The base record's Save and Load are Rust** (`rust_goal.rs` `base_save`, `base_load`): the action, the two flags,
  the id and both times, with the original's version gates (nothing after the action up to minor 14; before minor
  100, or after a failed read, the id is 0; a later major still reads the id only from minor 100; the second flag
  and the times from minor 135, 157 and 164). The dispatch runs it before every kind's own record but the heal goal's
  (which writes none), for ee_units' kinds and combat's alike, so ee_combat needed no change. The six fields cross by
  one host operation (495: read with `b` 0, write with `b` 1).
- **The world searches** (world.rs, over a `WorldHost` that `OpHost` implements; the `BuildHost`/`GatherHost` methods
  the bodies call keep their names and now run the Rust): `EEHelpBuildNearby`, `BuildFarms`' search,

  three footprint tests. A unit's fields come from the round-19 unit record (`EeUnitsBuildUnit`, which gained

## R5b.4, twenty-third round: EE-SIM's exit 2 and the one-message capture flake, both traced to start-up races (branch rust-r5b4-core23, 2026-11-13)

| Commit | What | C++ (src, include/ee) |
|---|---|---|
| 9430091c | EE-SIM waits for the lobby's combos to be filled before it selects (test only) | +16 -4 |
| 7aac1bae | the unit hack's box filled without its change event: no `EEMLoadUnitData` racing the game's start | +19 -3 |

No unit or player C++ moved this round: the brief said to stop at a real nondeterminism fix.

- **EE-SIM's exit 2 is `Fail`, and these runs failed in the lobby.** `Quit(2)` comes only from `Fail` (EESim.cpp:
  the report's `"outcome": "error"` and a `FAILED:` line on stdout, which `sim_oracle.py` keeps in `log-<seed>.txt`;
  a fault exits with its exception code instead). The UI lane's oracle seed 6 (162-byte trace) failed with `slot 0
  human: index #0 outside the combo's 0 lines`. The lobby's slot combos exist before their lines do: ee_screens
  `lobby_form.rs` `fill_player_types` clears and fills a slot's box when the local server's lobby update changes its
  menu. `SetUpLobby` waited only for the controls and then slept 1.5 s, so under load a selection could resolve over
  an empty box. The space capture's failed rerun (exit 2, a 66 KB capture) and the triggers lane's scenario seed 6
  (exit 2, 66 KB) stopped at the same point, before the game. `tools/sim_bench.py` already retried this error, but
  EE-SIM itself was never fixed. Now `SetUpLobby` waits until every slot box and the size, map and difficulty boxes
  have lines, and `Select` waits for an empty box's lines. `ScenarioFromLobby` waits until the game type box has a
  third line (index 2) and the difficulty box has lines. These are test-only waits: nothing in the game changed.
- **The extra executed message was the unit hack's `EEMLoadUnitData`.** Opening the main game form calls
  `EEUIFMGUnitHack::FillComboBox`, and its `SetCurrentSelection(0)` fired the box's change event (`EEUIELoadUnit`).
  That sent `EEMLoadUnitData` from the UI thread while the game was starting. A temporary print in
  `NESynchronousServer::ProcessLocalUserInput` showed it arriving in communications tick 26, one tick before
  `NEMStartGame` (27). `EEClient::HandleMessage` runs a CT's inputs as lobby input while its PT count is 0xff, and
  queues them for the physics once the CT has physics ticks. So an input that arrives one CT late runs in
  `EEPhysics::DrainInput` as a game input. That adds one NMEX, NMIM, NMDC (kind 3) and USCK record and one count
  to `mInputMessagesProcessed`, with no other digest changed. Every earlier sighting matches: the space seed 2
  capture (NMEX 9 to 10) and calamity seed 3 (3 to 4). The count also feeds the out-of-synch checksum and the AI
  trace's `sim hash ... inputs=` line, so the same race could make an oracle seed differ. The message's only effect
  is the sender's `mHackUnitClass` and that class's media, preloaded for every player.
  `EEMHackANewUnit` reads `mHackUnitClass` only when it carries no class, and the hack's own `PlaceUnit` always sends
  the listed class. `FillComboBox` now detaches the change event while it selects line 0 (with a reference held)
  and restores it afterwards. Changing the box later still sends the message.
- **What the reproduction ruled out.** I could not reproduce the extra message on demand. Four parallel space seed 2
  captures and four instrumented ones all gave the same 9 NMEX (6 `EEMReplantFarms` from the physics thread, 3
  `EEMCivTimerExpired`). Eight parallel calamity seed 3 games executed the same 3 messages at the same game ms.
  After the start, every `ProcessLocalUserInput` came from the physics thread. The wall-clock and keyboard senders
  cannot fire for EE-SIM's idle human: `ReportStatistics` (sent only when series 0x14/0x15 change, which only a
  human's clicks and hot keys do) and `CheckShiftMode` (needs `mShiftMode`). The number of CTs before the start
  varies by run (offsets of 1-6), but the simulation does not use it: `ApplyUpgradeLevel` and `SaveGame` read it
  into unused locals, and the autosave's `EEMLoadOrSaveGame` payload is the only place it reaches a message. The
  physics, AI and loading threads gave identical executed lists in all twelve games.
- **Tour only:** `FillComboBox` runs when the main game form opens. The tours open that form; EE-SIM opens it
  without drawing it. The hack class's media is no longer preloaded at the start.
- **Behaviour:** single-player and LAN games no longer send `EEMLoadUnitData` at the start. Nothing reaches the
  simulation: oracle seeds 2-7 are identical to `ref`, and the captures match their goldens.
- **Gates** (on the result, which already contained rust 57ae2ad1: the merge was a no-op): build `--sim` 0/0;
  oracle seeds 2-7 identical to the main checkout's `ref`; the Rust gate PASS; captures at seeds 2-3: oracle (169
  digests), late (170), space (171, NMEX 9 on seed 2), calamity (183) and scenario (16) PASS; the test profile 0/0. Before the fix, an instrumented build ran oracle seeds
  2-3 identical with no `0x71` sent. The saveload matrix was not run (nothing in Save, Load or RepairPointers
  changed).
- **For the next round:** the moves the brief named are still open (the unit classes' bodies through the unit store,
  or the player's per-tick code). The largest are `EEUnitClass`'s constructor (477 lines), `FindPath`/`AdjustPath`

| Function | Was (C++) | Now (Rust) |
|---|---|---|
| `EESMEffect`, `EESMCondition`, `EESMObject`, `EESMTrigger`'s numbers | members of each class | `EeScenario{Effect,Condition,Object,Trigger}Fields` (fields.rs), the classes' base: same names, same C++ types |
| `EESMEffect::Reset`, the condition's and object's constructors' numbers | 60 + 25 + 25 assignments | `effect_defaults`, `condition_defaults`, `object_defaults` |
| the three classes' `Copy` (numbers) | field by field | one assignment of the base record (strings and lists stay C++) |
| `Load` / `Save` of the effect, condition, object, trigger, area, media strings | 6 x 2 bodies, ~760 lines | save.rs over one I/O callback (`EeScenarioStream`, stream.rs) |
| the effect's, condition's, object's `Renumber*`, the entries' `Virtual4` | 13 bodies | `renumber` and the per-class lists (fields.rs) |
| `EESMEffect::SetAIVariable` and the 34 inline setters | a 480-line switch, 240 lines of setters | aivar.rs: the behaviours' stores as a table; the C++ applies them by field number (ee/EESMAIFields.h) |
| `EESMConditionRecord`, `EESMObjectFilter` (host) | C++ copies into Rust records | `From` the base records |

- **Records the C++ derives from.** `class EESMEffect : public EeScenarioEffectFields`: the cbindgen struct carries
  the members' own names (`mPlayer`, `mB193`, ...) and types (`c_ulong` is `unsigned long`, `c_long` `long`), so no
  reader changed: the editor screens, the capture, the effects' bodies all compile as before. A member's Rust type
  must be the C++ one exactly: `u32` would have broken every `unsigned long&` taker (`GetCurrentSelection(&...)`) and
  the LP64 width. Rust names in `mCamelCase` need `#![allow(non_snake_case)]` (fields.rs). The area keeps its
  members (a `U2DPoint`, a `GERectangle`); its save goes through a copy (`EeScenarioAreaSave`) filled and stored
  back by `EESMArea::SaveIO`.
- **The saves through one callback.** `EeScenarioStream::io(ctx, op, slot, index, value)`: each value is read or
  written by the C++ with the `FSFile` overload the original called (the 4-byte `long` adapters with their
  read-into-the-old-value semantics, `float`, `bool`), the strings by slot (`UWideString::Load/Save`), the id lists
  (`mObjects`, `mUnits`) and the trigger's entries (`SetCondition` + `SetConditionOperator`, which append an entry
  after a non-end operator on the last one) by operation. The Rust copies the record in, works on the copy, and
  stores it back after the last callback: no Rust reference lives across a call into C++. The `Seq` helper is the
  originals' `if (theResult == kErrorOK)` chains; the quirks are kept: a player action past the table moves down 2
  then to Victory whatever the read gave, the condition's chat text result is ignored, the diplomacy clamp runs even
  after a failed read, the object appends its units (no clear), the effect replaces its list, the trigger's entry
  locals carry from one entry to the next and an id of -1 becomes 0, the effects' count is written only after no
  error, the area's anchor is stored (cut toward zero) only when both floats read and its rectangle only when all four.
- **SMSV, the golden for the saves** (ee/EEScenarioCapture.h, recorded from the unmodified C++ first): after
  `EEScenarioManager::Load` and every 120th trigger round, each list's count, first error and FNV of its elements'
  `Save` into an `FSMemoryFile` (the built-ins included, which the manager's own Save skips), then the whole
  manager's `Save`. Six scenarios, 25-29 records each. A load and a save both wrong in a matching way would still
  differ from the C++'s bytes.
- **Set AI Variable's golden driver.** `build/trig_draft/gen_aivar_driver.py` (TEST ONLY scratch, not committed)

## LLE Network Engine, round 1: the census, NEMessageManager whole in Rust (ee_net msgmgr.rs; branch rust-ne1, 2026-11-13)

The lane's goal is the whole Low-Level Engine in Rust as whole classes; this round's part is the Network Engine
(`src/Low-Level Engine/Network Engine`, `include/lle/NE*.h`). Already Rust before it: the TCP transport
(`ee_net_tcp`, R3.3) and the 28 engine messages' wire codec (`ee_netmsg` engine.rs).

**The census** (at e551a6d7; code lines = neither blank nor comment; callers = files outside the Network Engine and
its headers that name the class):

| Class (unit) | .cpp code | header code | Not a one-line forwarder | Callers | Subclasses | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NEMessage + 27 engine messages (NEMessage.cpp) | 897 | 548 | ~600 (ctors, IsResponse, Execute, the factory; the codec is Rust) | 156 | EEMessage's 104 game classes | the hub type of both lockstep sides; next to last |
| NESynchronousServer | 1,184 | 292 | ~1,100 (ctor, three threads, tuning, OOS, booting) | 36 | EEServer | 19 pure virtuals the game implements |
| NESynchronousClient | 544 | 130 | ~500 (two threads, connect, tick dispatch) | 29 | EEClient | 14 pure virtuals |
| NEMessageManager | 590 | 79 | all | 0 (NESynchronousServer only, as friend) | none | **moved this round** |
| NEProtocol + NEConnection + NEServer | 196 | 154 | ~120 (ctor's GetEntry table, byte counters, Accept/Close wrappers); NEConnection/NEServer all inline forwarders | 8 | none | the plug-in's entry table over ee_net_tcp |
| NEProtocolConfiguration | 282 | 44 | all | 0 in the game (the TCP shim's gConfiguration and tcp_test only; no caller of Get/SetConfiguration) | none | a 0-parameter table nobody reads |
| NERecordPlayback | 235 | 48 | all | 3 (EEMessage's slow/normal playback, the mode tests) | none | always in pass mode in a normal game |
| NELagLossSimulator | 189 | 61 | all | 0 outside the client | none | off unless enabled (no caller enables it) |
| NETimestampedMessage | 43 | 19 | 3 functions | 0 outside NELagLossSimulator / NERecordPlayback | none | goes with those two |
| NESynchronousCommunications | 51 | 62 | 2 (the byte-rate meters) | 138 (gCommunications) | the server, the client | abstract base; stays the type callers hold |
| NEPlayer | 0 | 23 | (all inline) | 0 (included, never used) | none | dead |
| Network Engine.cpp (NEInitialize/NEShutdown) | 30 | - | 2 | 2 | - | |
| TCP Protocol.cpp | 261 | - | the NPIM shim (UString/TSEvent conversion) | - | - | ee_net_tcp behind it |

Order, best deletion-to-risk first, bottom-up: NEMessageManager (done); NEPlayer (dead); NEProtocolConfiguration
(no game reader: the plug-in's table can become a Rust value with Get/SetConfiguration's two entries); NETimestampedMessage
with NELagLossSimulator and NERecordPlayback (client-side queues and a thread each, three callers); NEProtocol's table
(the plug-in is Rust: the entry table can call ee_net_tcp directly); then the client and the server state machines
(threads, lockstep tuning: RUST_PLAN 2.1), and NEMessage last (156 callers, the game's base class).

**The move** (`rust/crates/ee_net`, a new crate: `msgmgr.rs`, `rlock.rs`, `ffi.rs`): the ring of the last 50 sent
messages (each message held by reference, the slots that still owe it an answer, its time, its count of answers
owed), the clients (ten response times and their average, the CPU load and its 240-entry history, the lowest tick),
the per-slot transfer queues (each transfer's own copy of the file spec, its state, bytes, retries, abort flag) and
the counters, with every method of NEMessageManager.cpp and the server's `GetSlowestClientCPU` (which read the
clients). NEMessageManager.cpp and lle/NEMessageManager.h are deleted; NESynchronousServer holds an `EeNetMsgMgr*`
and calls `ee_net_mm_*`; its static `MessageManagerHost` answers the 28 ops (`EeNetMmOp`: the messages' Reference,
Dereference, type, IsResponse, slot, export-and-send; the server's three responses; the server members the manager
read and wrote; its two events; TMGetTime; HandleXferStatus; an NEMXferMessage sent by XferSendTo; the file spec's
copy, free, open, close, length, read and name).

- **Locks.** The original's two critical sections (Win32's, re-entrant) are two re-entrant locks (`rlock.rs`), held
  where the original held them: `LogResponse` and `StoreSentMessage` across their message calls, the transfer pass
  across its sends and status reports. The re-entrance is real: a transfer's status reaches the game
  (`EEServer::HandleXferStatus` -> `ProcessLocalUserInput` -> ... `ProcessSystemMessage`), which may queue another
  transfer on the same thread. The state the original touched without a lock (the clients, the ring's slot maps in
  Send/Resend/RegisterSlot) is touched under its lock here, never across a call out: no Rust reference lives across a
  host call (each borrow is a closure over the state that makes no call).
- **Iteration across calls out.** Send, Resend and the transfer pass walked `std::map`s while calling out; the Rust
  walks by key (the next key after the last one visited, read again after each call), which is what the original's
  iterator did for every change a call could make (values changed, keys added) and is defined where the original's
  was not (a key erased under it).
- **Behaviour changes, on undefined or crashing paths only:** `WhoHasNotRespondedNext` from a slot that is not
  registered answers none (the original stepped past `end()`); a transfer whose status report removed its queue or
  itself stops that slot's step (the original used the freed objects); a transfer's start block holds any file name
  (the original copied it into a 1 KB stack buffer); a resend of a ring entry that never held a message (after
  `SetMessageManagerCurrentMessageNumber` moved the number past the stored ones) sends nothing (the original sent
  NULL); transfers still queued when the server is freed release their file specs (the original leaked them). The
  32-bit `unsigned long` arithmetic (times, ticks, numbers) is `u32` wrapping as on Windows.
- **The golden** (`tests/net/ne_msgmgr_test.cpp`, `python -I tools/xbuild.py nettest`, new): the original
  NEMessageManager.cpp, unmodified (`tests/net/orig/NEMessageManager.cpp`, with its header), compiled over stand-in
  headers in `tests/net/orig/lle/` (a quoted include finds the includer's directory first): a world of messages (a
  type, a key, a slot, references; a response answers the type before it with the same key), files (name, length,
  position), events, the protocol server and the server members, each effect a trace line and each answer (a send's
  result, a file's open and read) from the side's random stream. The Rust side's host answers with the same world
  objects, statement for statement as NESynchronousServer's host. 20,000 sequences of 80 random steps (sends,
  sends to one slot, send-to-all-and-wait, responses, response times, queries, resends, the lag walk, transfers
  queued, aborted and advanced, slots registered and removed, the clock and server members changed) and a teardown
  (every slot removed, the manager freed, every message given back): 8,236,415 trace lines, all equal. Mutations of
  the Rust:

  | Mutation | Sequences differing |
  |---|---|
  | LogResponse marks every matching entry (no break) | 276 |
  | a broadcast owes one answer fewer | 8,327 |
  | the response-time average over nine | 1 |
  | the transfer status every second instead of two | 444 |
  | the lag walk's next from the previous slot itself | 11,787 |
  | an unregistered slot's answered entry counted out too | 346 |

  The retry limit (1,000 failed starts before an abort) is out of the golden's reach. The first driver hung on the
  "next" mutation (the walk never advanced and the trace grew to 10 GB): the walk is now capped at six steps.
- **Cargo:** the Rust side's host also records each op with its arguments and answer (messages and files by world
  id); the first 100 sequences are `golden_msgmgr.txt` (0.9 MB), which `tests.rs` replays against the Rust alone
  (each op must be the next recorded one). The replay fails on the broadcast and status-interval mutations; a unit
  test covers the ring's 50-entry window, the lag walk from an unknown slot and the release of queued transfers.
- **What runs it.** Every game runs the server's manager: the single-player game's local server sends each
  communications tick through `Send` (the server's own slot registered, the tick handled as its own message, its
  response logged), so the oracle exercises the ring, the response times and the tick responses: seeds 2-7 identical
  to `ref`. The clients' slots, resends, the lag report, booting, send-to-all-and-wait (pause, save) and file
  transfers (a saved game sent to joining players) run only in a LAN game: `lan_game.py` (see the gates table) and,
  for transfers and pausing, only the golden unless a person loads a saved multiplayer game.
- **Gates** (the round's head, a8582dc5 + docs; rust 5d3ce6a9 is already in the branch, so the merge was a no-op):
  build --sim 0/0 (EE-AOC and EE-SIM) after each commit; oracle seeds 2-7 identical to ref after the first and the
  last commit; the Rust gate PASS; the test-profile build 0/0; tcp_test passes without NEProtocolConfiguration;
  lan_game.py on the final test exe: RESULT PASS lan-game, PT host 2942 joiner 2941 (60 s of play, CTs equal at
  every 5 s sample within 2). No capture or saveload run: nothing in the tick path or the saved state moved (NMNE
  covers the engine messages' codec, which this round did not touch).
- **NEPlayer deleted** (its own commit): the header-only class had no user; four units included it.
- **NEProtocolConfiguration deleted** (its own commit): the game never called `NEProtocol::GetConfiguration` /
  `SetConfiguration`; the class's only instance was the TCP shim's `gConfiguration(0, 1)`, a table of no parameters
  handed out as copies to nobody. The class, the two NPIM entries (`NPIMGetConfiguration`, `NPIMSetConfiguration`),
  NEProtocol's two members and lookups, and six includes went; `tcp_test` links without the unit.
- **Commits, net C++ over src + include (without include/rust):** NEMessageManager -804 (+180, -984); NEPlayer -33;
  NEProtocolConfiguration -428 (+2, -430). Round: -1,265.
- **Lessons:** the Bash tool turns a two-character `\n` inside a heredoc into a newline: Python edit scripts with
  escapes go through the Write tool as a file. A golden driver that loops until a value changes must cap the loop: a
  mutation that stops the change otherwise eats the machine's memory.

## R4.4, fifteenth round: the additive pass, the linear projectile, the disease and the virus whole in Rust on EEE3DRust (ee_gfx effect_additive.rs, effect_orbit.rs; branch rust-gfx21, 2026-11-13)

Graphics Thread C++ (`src/Empire Earth/Graphics Thread/*.cpp`): 21,643 lines before the round; 21,446 after the
additive pass (-197); 21,220 after the linear projectile (-226); 20,627 after the disease and virus (-593).
`EEE3DAdditivePass`, `EEE3DLinearProjectile`, `EEE3DDisease` and `EEE3DVirus` (`.cpp` and `.h`) deleted. All four
kinds were already in round 14's effects sweep (0x27 on a unit, 0x25 between points, 0x23 and 0x42 on a unit), so
no sweep extension was needed: each move is checked against the original C++'s golden in a game world.

- **The additive pass (0x27, `effect_additive.rs`).** The unit's own model of its animation redrawn in pass 5
  (one-one blending, z test only, white lighting dimmed by the fog factor at its place, the effect's texture on the
  model's first material, the fog restored after), queued in 3 with the unit's frame, animation, transformation and
  scale; it follows the unit's stats' scale and location every step (7 at zero hit points). `EEE3DRust` gains
  `mUnitModel` (the unit's `EEModel`, loaded by `SetUp` and `RepairPointers`, unloaded by the destructor). The host
  gains the unit's model media, scale, location, model radius, frame and animation, and model by index; the table
  `SetGraphicsCurrentFrame`. `EEEffect3D(long)`, which the original emitted in `EEE3DAdditivePass.cpp`, is in
  `EEEffect3D.cpp` now. Record part: `pass` (`EeGfxEffectPass`).
- **The orbitals in Rust (`effect_orbit.rs`).** `EEOrbital` copies of the graphic object's (the host's
  `orbital_count`/`orbital`: model, speed, angle) are a Rust list the record owns (`orbit.orbitals`, a `Box` made on
  first use, freed by `ee_gfx_effect_record_free`), with `mOrbitalCount` (`orbit.count`) and the draw's angles.
  `EEOrbital::Update` is `EeGfxOrbital::update` (the same f32 ops and wrap); each orbital's model gets its
  pre-model transformation from `set_orientation(Ypr, angle, 0, 0)` (a new table entry). The projectile's set-up and
  Load draw one effect random per orbital in order (the RNG is checked by EFST's seed).
- **The linear projectile (0x25).** A new `EEE3DRust(from, to, graphic effect, kind)` constructor (the manager's
  `CreateEffectBetween`): the line, the speed of about one duration (one random draw), the step along the line (7
  past its end at 1), queue 3, the prelit pass-5 draw fading over the last fifth; Load and Save of position, speed and
  line on the shot part (format unchanged). The constructor's "to" travels in `shot.location`, zeroed after, as the
  original's `mLocation` was until the first queue.
- **The disease (0x23) and the virus (0x42).** Animation 13 of the graphic object (the host's `animation`: start
  frame, frame time, frame count), the frame advance (`UMFloatToLong` is `ee_ge::um::lrintf`; the frame products
  wrapping u32 as the C++'s unsigned long), the age over the duration on the aged record (7 at a dead unit or past
  1), the disease on its unit's location, the virus on its first tag point (`FollowUnit`) with its u scroll by
  param 1 (wrapped to 0..1), the orbitals turned, and the animation's sound at the unit (the host's
  `animation_sound`: `PlayAnimationSound`, `SetSound` and the extra dereference exactly as the original; the sound is
  `EEE3DRust::mSound`, stopped and released by the destructor). Pass 5: z test and write, alpha blended, unit
  lighting (the disease sets the shading source, the virus does not), the frame, scale, the virus's u scroll (new
  table entries `model_scroll_u`/`model_restore_u`, twins of the shield's v), the orbitals, fading over the last
  tenth. Load and Save of time, frame, age and the virus's scroll (format unchanged).
- **Golden drivers** (`build/gx21/drv/make.py COMMIT|WORKTREE OUT KINDS`: the original classes cut from d8f1de16, or
  `EEE3DRust`'s host, constructors, `Call`, `RepairPointers` and the rasterizer table cut from the worktree over the
  Rust; round 14's aged driver's stub world plus the unit's stats and model, `SetGraphicsCurrentFrame` and
  `SetGraphicsPreModelTransform`, the graphic object's orbitals and animation 13, `EEOrbital::Update` cut from
  `EEOrbital.cpp`, sounds, u texture coordinates, a tag-point list). Ops per effect: construction, set-up, then
  random steps, queues, pass 5, passes 2/4/6, `RepairPointers` and moves of the unit; the state printed after each.
  Identical bytes: additive 300 effects (6,793 lines) and 3,000 on seed 2 (68,081); projectile 300 (6,479) and
  3,000 (67,940); disease and virus 300 (6,819) and 3,000 (67,781; 6,024 sounds, 670 fades, 1,531 viruses); the four
  together on the final tree 300 (6,566) and 3,000 (68,099). Rust tests: 3 additive, 8 orbit (the orbital's wrap,
  each kind's set-up/step/queue, draws, Load and Save).
- **Lesson (tooling):** this shell collapses a doubled backslash inside heredocs; Python edit scripts with escapes must be written
  as files with the editor, not piped through a heredoc.
- **Behaviour:** none intended (each commit's effects capture equals the golden recorded from the original C++).
  One hardening: a graphic whose animation 13 has zero frames gives frame 0 instead of the C++'s divide by zero.
- **Gates.** On the result merged with rust (1f4b8a50): `build.py --sim` and the test profile link 0/0, the Rust gate PASS (2,681 tests), the sim oracle identical on seeds 2-7, the captures at seeds 2-3 PASS (oracle 169 digests, late 170, calamity 183, effects 6), `saveload --settings all --seeds 2-3 --at 1000,1900 --expect tools/saveload_expect.txt` PASS (the matrix as expected). Per commit: the build 0/0, the oracle at seeds 2-3 identical, the effects capture at seeds 2-3 PASS against the C++ golden, the Rust gate PASS (2,645, 2,649, 2,653 tests; on the third commit two load-timing tests outside ee_gfx failed in the full run, `ee_gx`'s bind-group test and `ee_plat_core`'s timer tests, each passing alone; the gate was then run with `--no-fail-fast`: every crate's tests, clippy, rustfmt and the header check PASS). The drivers were run on each move's commit; the merge touched no file they cut. No tour run.
- **Only a tour or a person reaches:** every draw of the four kinds through the table (the additive pass's
  one-one redraw of a unit's model and the fog it restores; the projectile's and disease's alpha-blended models with
  turning orbital parts; the virus's u-scrolled texture and its restore: a missing restore would leave the model's
  texture shifted for every later draw of that model), the animation sounds of the disease and virus (EE-SIM has no
  sound), and a saved game holding one of them loaded whole.
- **Next:** the hurricane (0x24: orbitals and a sound like the virus, the same host calls) after extending the sweep
  to it (golden from f839d277 in a temporary worktree, as round 14), the energy wave, nuclear explosion and goal;
  the 2D twin (`EEE2DRust` over `EEEffect2D`) for the sprite effects.

## R4.3, seventh part: the census, GEModelManager and GETextureManager whole in Rust (ee_ge manobj.rs, texobj.rs; branch rust-ge-next, 2026-11-13)

The Graphics Engine's first whole-class round. Parts one to six moved its math, geometry, plans and text to Rust and
left every class a C++ shell around them; this round measures what C++ is left per class and moves the first two
classes whole, in the WON lane's pattern (PORT_LEARNINGS "R6 WON round 26"-"30").

| Commit | What | C++ (`git diff --numstat` over src, include/lle, include/ee) |
|---|---|---|
| 02b6e78b | the census tool; the store gate reads the texture cache through accessors and links again | +9 -1, net +8 |
| 6f6f53df | GEModelManager whole in Rust (`manobj.rs`) | +121 -125, net -4 |
| 8b6106fa | GETextureManager whole in Rust (`texobj.rs`) | +254 -291, net -37 |

- **The census** (`tools/ge_census.py`): per unit, its code lines and the lines of its bodies that are not one-line
  forwarders (more than two statements, or two without a call into Rust). At the round's start (logic lines of 3,666;
  5,982 code lines in 37 units): GESurface 663, GETexture 418, GETerrainMesh 394, GEModel 372 (+120 in
  'GEModel Load.cpp'), GERasterizer 260, GETextureManager 232, GEBitmap 188, GETransformation 137 (its constructors'
  member copies), GEFontBitmap 129, GEModelManager 99, GEOpenFormatsFile 83; every other unit under 81. After it:
  GETextureManager 182 and GEModelManager 66, nearly all of it the hosts' call tables (one switch each, which the
  census counts as one logic body).
- **Why the managers, and in this order.** The candidates named for the round were GECamera (no such class: the
  camera is the game's EECamera), GELight (a header-only record the renderer reads field by field: nothing to move),
  GEFont and GEText (no logic left after part six), GETexture/GETextureManager and GEModel/GEModelManager. What blocks
  a whole move is subclasses and members read outside the class (`build/ge7/fields.py`, scratch: a header's members
  named with `->`/`.` in files that also name the class, an upper bound): GESurface has a subclass (DX7Surface) and
  its logic is the BMP and JPEG codecs of screenshots; GETexture's members are named in 91 outside files, GEModel's in
  21 (the renderer, the effects and the graphic objects read their frames, stages, arrays and tag points),
  GETerrainMesh's in 141, GERasterizer is DX7Rasterizer's base. The two managers have no subclass and private members
  only (outside readers: their friends, GETexture's `RemoveTexture`/`PromoteTexture` calls and the store gate's
  digest), and they own the models and textures (a model or texture object lives in its manager's cache): the leaves
  of the ownership graph, so bottom-up they come first. GEModelManager first (smaller: the pattern), then its twin.
- **The pattern.** One Rust object per manager (`EeGeModelManager`, `EeGeTextureManager`): the cache (a `BTreeMap` of
  the name's bytes: `strcmp` order, as the original's `std::map<UString, ...>` with `UString::operator<`), the path
  (held), the lock, the footprint (`c_ulong`, wrapping like the original's `unsigned long`) and the screen. The C++
  class's only member is `mRust`; its methods are one-line forwarders; its copy is deleted. Every call the original
  made on another object is one host operation (`EeGeManOp`; `GEModelManager::Host`, `GETextureManager::Host`,
  private static members so they keep the classes' friend access to GEModel's and GETexture's privates), in the
  original's order: the lock (the engine's `TSCriticalSection`, kept: it is recursive, and a load may come back into
  its manager on the same thread), the path's references, the constructors, `SetSubModel`, `StoreLoaded`, `Load`,
  `SizeOf`, `GetAllocatedSize`, the stage setters, the base `Dereference`, the reference count, the file lookups and
  frees and the dump's `fprintf`s. A texture's fields the original read or wrote directly (`mIsFromTexturePack`,
  `mTexturePackMipLevels`, `mNumMipLevelsToDrop`, `mIsManaged`, its stage) are host operations too (`EeGeTexField`,
  `EeGeTexStage`, both and `EeGeTexLoad` in cbindgen.toml's `include`: no exported function names them).
- **Calls back in.** No Rust reference to an object lives across a host call (each access is one statement through
  the raw pointer), and every walk of a cache goes by key, to the entry after the current name: an insertion or
  another entry's removal by a callee leaves the walk where the original's `std::map` iterator would be.
- **The surface description** is a `#[repr(C)]` mirror (`EeGeSurfaceDescription`; GETextureManager.cpp
  `static_assert`s its size and offsets against `GESurfaceDescription`, and the texture description's mirror
  against `GETextureDescription`). `GETexture::Load` writes into it, and `RefreshAllTextures` keeps one for every
  texture as the original's local did: a `mNoAlpha` a load wrote reaches the next texture's load (a mutation that
  starts each texture with a fresh description changes 5,938 golden sequences).
- **The goldens** (scratch, `build/ge7/golden`: `build.py mod|tex orig|cur`, `mutate.py`): the manager's unit of the
  census commit 02b6e78b (unmodified, by `git show`) or the worktree's, its engine includes replaced by traced fakes
  (`fake_ge.h`, `fake_tex.h`: models, textures with frames, stages and surfaces, paths, the lock, the file lookups,
  a `UString` in `strcmp` order) and linked with a scratch staticlib of `ee_ge`. Random sequences of every method and
  of the callers' own actions (references taken and given back; `GETexture::Dereference` from a holder, which calls
  `RemoveTexture`; `Promote`; the texture pack's settings), with calls back into the manager from inside a load; the
  texture driver traces every live texture's fields after each call. GEModelManager: 20,000 sequences, 3,668,661
  trace lines; GETextureManager: 20,000 sequences, 7,397,266 lines. Relinked over the shells and the Rust objects,
  both print the same per-sequence digests. The first 40 sequences are `golden_modman.txt` and `golden_texman.txt`,
  which cargo replays through a mock host keeping a world of the objects (reference counts, texture fields,
  surfaces) from the trace's lines (`manobj_tests.rs`, `texobj_tests.rs`); the replays fail on a Rust mutation (four
  checked: the footprint's subtraction, RemoveAll's result, the pack shift, the pack name's stem).

  | Golden | Mutation of the Rust | Sequences of 20,000 that change |
  |---|---|---|
  | models | RemoveModel answers 3 for a model in use | 11,081 |
  | | a removal adds its size to the footprint | 10,724 |
  | | RemoveAllModels answers the last decision | 5,866 |
  | | SetModelPath holds the new path before releasing the old | 10,847 |
  | | LoadModel misses cached models | 19,559 |
  | | a load adds nothing to the footprint | 12,714 |
  | | a failed store keeps the model | 19,595 |
  | textures | a reload keeps the old size in the footprint | 636 |
  | | the refresh holds no frames | 19,885 |
  | | the refresh copies the min filter before the mag filter | 9,400 |
  | | the pack is asked for the name, not its stem | 3,348 |
  | | a cached texture's reload ignores its pack | 19,600 |
  | | a made texture is not managed | 19,992 |
  | | the refresh starts each texture with a fresh description | 5,938 |
  | | UpdateMIPFilterMode sets every texture | 9,165 |
  | | a pack texture's logical shift is not set | 5,460 |

  The restored source changes 0 in both. A panic in the mock host cannot unwind through the object's `extern "C"`
  host call (the test process aborted): the hosts catch it and the replay reports it after the call returns.
- **Two undefined paths of the original the fakes avoid**, both in `RefreshAllTextures`: the frame list is one
  `std::vector` for all textures, read after the load with the load's frame count (a load that adds frames reads
  stale or missing entries: the fakes' reloads never add frames; the Rust reads a missing entry as NULL instead of
  past the vector); and a frame-format-1 texture's `GetFrameTexture` is its `mFrames[0]`, which `Load` does not set
  for that format. When it is the texture itself, its `Dereference` at the last outside reference removes it from the
  cache under the walk: the original then stepped from a freed node (the first fakes did this and the two sides
  parted at sequence 43), the Rust goes on with the next name. The fakes give a grid texture a frame of its own.
- **Behaviour changes:** none on the original's defined paths. LoadModel's two `TSScheduler::GetCurrentThreadIndex`
  calls (results unused) are gone; `GetTextureAt` past the end is NULL; the two undefined refresh paths above.
- **The counters** of made textures and created models stay process-wide (`managers.rs`). The replays set them from
  the trace (the driver's `ext made N`, a created model's name) under `managers::test_globals`, a lock the counters'
  and the texture pack's own tests now take too.
- **The store gate links again** (census commit): the mixer's objects pull in ee_sound's music, whose C++ side
  (`ee_musiccpp_*`) is the game's; the gate links with `/FORCE:UNRESOLVED` and fails on any other unresolved
  symbol. It passes after each move: every model and texture of the open tree through LoadModel, LoadTexture,
  ReloadTexture and RefreshAllTextures, 25,140 lines equal to the recorded digests.
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM does: a temporary count of host operations in an oracle run (removed) showed both
  managers creating, loading, sizing, removing, refreshing (`TexSurfaceDescription`) and setting stages; the oracle
  stayed identical. The store gate runs every real file through them. Only the game runs the paths that need a
  device or a person: textures made from the screen's surfaces (`MakeTexture` for the UI's surfaces), the device
  loss refresh, `UpdateMIPFilterMode` from the settings, `DumpAllLoadedMedia`, and the texture pack's log
  (`EE_TEXTURE_PACK_LOG`, posix_game.py's evidence). The lead's tour and menu pixel comparison check the textures
  and models drawn.
- **Lessons:**
  - Python's `write_text` on Windows writes CRLF (round 26's lesson): a scripted edit turned two Rust files and
    `rust/cbindgen.toml` into CRLF before the commit (caught by `file`); use `read_bytes`/`write_bytes`.
  - The Bash tool's heredocs lose backslashes (`\n` inside a Python string became a newline, a regex lost its
    escapes): edit text with backslashes through the editor tool, not a heredoc.
  - A class whose methods are mostly calls on other objects keeps about as many C++ lines as a host as it had as
    methods: the gain is the decisions, walks and state in Rust (and the goldens), not the line count.
- **Gates.** Each move: build `--sim` 0/0 (EE-AOC and EE-SIM), `rust_build.py gate` PASS, the oracle identical on
  seeds 2-3, the store gate PASS (25,140 lines). At the round's end (`rust` had not moved since 5d3ce6a9, which the
  branch's base already holds: nothing to merge): the oracle identical on seeds 2-7, the captures at seeds 2-3 PASS
  (oracle 169, late 170, calamity 183 digests; TNMT has no golden in any of them, as before this round), the test
  profile 0/0, the Rust gate PASS. Nothing saved moved (the managers are not in a save): no saveload matrix. Not run:
  any harness session (the tour, the menu pixel comparison, the LAN game), macOS or Linux builds.
- **The merge of `rust`** (57ae2ad1: WON round 31, the LLE lane's round 1, the renderer's round 14, combat 15, core 21;
  it moved during the round): only the docs and cbindgen.toml's `include` list conflicted (both sides appended).
  `rust_includes.py` gave the two manager headers `rust/ee_ge.h` in place of their forward declarations of the Rust
  object and `EeGeManOp` (kept, its own commit: the tool's convention, as `GETextureSet.h`'s, so the next run leaves
  them alone; every unit including a manager header now sees ee_ge's header) and re-added `rust/ee_screens.h` to the
  two scenario editor files (not committed). On the merged tree: build `--sim` 0/0, the Rust gate PASS, the store
  gate PASS, the oracle identical on seeds 2-7, the captures at seeds 2-3 PASS (oracle 169, calamity 183; late failed
  once on seed 3's message counts, NMEX/NMIM 5 -> 6 with NMDC and USCK one more, the load flake PORT_LEARNINGS
  records for calamity seed 3, and passed with 170 on a rerun), the test profile 0/0.
- **Left** (by the census): GESurface (codecs; a subclass), GETexture and GEModel (accessors for their outside
